h1: Senfeng tube lasers — two-chuck T series to four-chuck heavy-duty machines, Ø0.5″ to 25″, the value line
intro: Senfeng's tube lasers are the value line of NovoTech's tube laser section, sold under the Senfeng brand: thirty models that start where most shops start — a 6 m two-chuck machine with a 1.5 kW source for the railings, frames, furniture and racking tube that make up most tube work — and go where few others do. The T series two-chuck machines cover Ø0.5 to 14″ and 20 to 39 ft with 1.5 to 6 kW; the PLUS runs to 492 ft/min on small tube and the GPLUS / GT add a 45° bevel head for mitred corners and weld preparations; the NT puts a third chuck in the middle so the last part is cut without a tail; and the ST three-chuck and HT four-chuck machines carry tube to Ø25″ and 6,600 lb over 29 to 49 ft with 6 to 20 kW, for structural steel, towers, cranes and trailers. The SF1500CH is the profile line for H-beams, channels and angles. Pneumatic self-centring chucks, following supports, tube nesting from 3D files, bundle loaders and unloading conveyors; CE / FDA / ETL certified. Installed, trained and supported from Mississauga, ON, Canada, with a CSA-approved panel and NovoTech's warranty.

groups.title: Senfeng tube lasers — the value line
groups.lead: Thirty models from the Ø0.5″ two-chuck T series to four-chuck machines for Ø25″ tube and H-beams.

faq.a: The T series is the all-round two-chuck machine: 1.5 to 6 kW, Ø0.5 to 14″, 20 to 39 ft, fifteen models — the one most shops buy first. The PLUS is tuned for speed on small and medium tube — 394 to 492 ft/min, 180 rpm chucks, 3 to 6 kW — for furniture, fitness equipment and racking where thousands of short parts are cut a shift. If you also need mitres and weld preparations, the GPLUS (Ø0.6 – 4.7″) or GT (Ø2.3 – 14.1″) add the 45° bevel head.

faq.q: What is zero-tailing — the NT series?
faq.a: A two-chuck machine cannot cut the last part of the bar because the rear chuck has to hold something, so a remnant of the chuck length is scrapped from every bar. The NT puts a third chuck in the middle that takes over the bar as it shortens, so the last part is cut and the tail is near zero — on 20 to 39 ft stock to Ø14″ that is several percent of material saved on every bundle.

faq.q: When do I need three or four chucks — ST and HT?
faq.a: When the tube is long and heavy: the ST (three chucks) and HT (four chucks) carry tube to Ø25″ and 6,600 lb over 29 to 49 ft without sag, so round, square and large rectangular sections for structural steel, towers, cranes and trailers are cut straight and square. Sources of 6 to 20 kW cut walls to 3/4″; bevel heads and automatic loaders are available. The SF1500CH is the version for H-beams, channels and angles, with a camera that scans each beam before cutting.

faq.q: How is the tube loaded and unloaded?
faq.a: From a bundle: the automatic loader separates one bar, measures it and feeds it to the rear chuck; the front chuck and the following supports hold the bar as it is cut; finished parts drop onto the unloading table or conveyor and the remnant is ejected. The loader is optional on the small T series — many shops start with manual loading — and standard on the heavy machines.

The bus-based CNC imports STEP / IGES solid models or draws the parts in its own tube CAD, unfolds them onto the profile, nests them along the bar to use the remnant and writes the program, with a cutting database for the material and seam detection to orient welded tube. Offline programming on a PC is standard.

faq.q: How does Senfeng compare with the Dener premium line?
faq.a: Dener's E-FTL and FTL are the premium machines — Turkish-built, 1 G servo chucks, Precitec heads, Dener Canada parts in Mississauga, ON, Canada. Senfeng costs a fraction of that for the same tube sizes and reaches further: zero-tailing three-chuck machines, four-chuck machines for 49 ft stock, Ø25″ pipe and the H-beam line. The comparison and the capacity table for both lines are on the tube laser cutters overview.

faq.q: What voltage do these machines run on?
faq.a: Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models with a small enough motor. Manual machines have no electrics.
